items.title: Steam’s Cyberpunk Fest is live with huge discounts on futuristic PC games
items.summary: Steam’s Cyberpunk Fest is live now through August 10, featuring a wide variety if discounted cyberpunk-themed games, demos, and upcoming titles.
items.content:
Steam has kicked off another themed event, and this week's spotlight belongs to Cyberpunk Fest. Running for the next seven days, the sale celebrates everything from dystopian RPGs and futuristic shooters to neon-soaked city builders inspired by classics like Blade Runner. Alongside hefty discounts, the event also includes free demos and a showcase of upcoming cyberpunk-themed releases.

As with every major Steam festival, Valve has released one of its trademark trailers hosted by Kaci Aitchison, offering a quick look at some of the featured games while injecting the company's usual sense of humor.

Unsurprisingly, Cyberpunk 2077 is front and center. Although the RPG had already gone on sale ahead of the festival, it's still one of the biggest deals available. The base game can now be picked up for $17.99 / 17,99€ / £14.99 after a 70% discount, while the Ultimate Edition, which bundles in the Phantom Liberty expansion, has dropped to $33.10 / 33,10€ / £27.58, saving players 60%.

One of the more interesting indie picks is Katanaut , which blends metroidvania exploration, roguelite progression, and cosmic horror into a stylish cyberpunk setting. Players explore a ruined space station, unlock new abilities, and carve through terrifying creatures with a shadow-powered blade. During the event, it's available for just $5.57 / 5,42€ / £4.63, a 69% discount.

Another standout is Peripeteia , an immersive sim set in an alternate-history version of Poland. Mixing first- and third-person gameplay with stealth, RPG systems, and shooter mechanics, it offers a fresh take on the genre. It's currently 25% off, bringing the price down to $18.21 / 17,93€ / £15.38.

There are plenty of other notable discounts worth checking out as well. RoboCop: Rogue City has been slashed by 90%, both Deus Ex: Human Revolution – Director's Cut and Deus Ex: Mankind Divided are available at 85% off, while Ninja Gaiden 4 has received a 40% discount.

If you aren't familiar with Steam's regular themed festivals, these events are frequent occurrences on Valve’s popular PC gaming platform, designed to spotlight specific genres. They’ve grown increasingly common recently, frequently coordinated directly by developers and publishers. These sales are an excellent opportunity to discover titles that might have escaped your attention, particularly while waiting for the broader scope of the well-known Steam Next Fest.

Steam Cyberpunk Fest runs until August 10, giving PC gamers a full week to browse the discounts before the event comes to a close. As always, if you’re looking to get the most value from your gaming budget, be sure to browse our dedicated deals hub for the latest offers.

items.title: 5 Best Video Games To Play While Waiting For Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet
items.summary: "Intergalactic" will be the next big hit from Naughty Dog, but gamers have a while yet to wait. Check out these five great sci-fi games to pass the time.
items.content:
Sony Interactive Entertainment Gamers have been waiting for a brand new title from Naughty Dog for a long time. The company's last major new release was "The Last of Us: Part II" back in 2020 (not counting the recent remasters), and fans haven't gotten a new IP from the developer in longer than most of us can remember. Since then the company has cancelled "The Last of Us Online" and released those aforementioned remasters, but fans are ready for something new.

Luckily, they won't have to wait that much longer. Naughty Dog revealed "Intergalactic: The Heretic" with a trailer in December 2024, and recent reporting suggests that the company is looking at an early 2027 release date for the final game. Finally, fans are getting the new IP they've been wanting, and they're going to experience an entirely new sci-fi universe along with it.

We don't yet know much about what the actual gameplay in "Intergalactic" will entail. The reveal trailer showed us a tiny bit of spaceship flight and some futuristic swordplay, and if those small details made you as excited to play "Intergalactic" as we are, then these five games might help you survive the wait.

Sony Interactive Entertainment "Returnal" is a sci-fi roguelike game that's sure to help you kill dozens of hours while waiting for Naughty Dog's "Intergalactic." Developed by Housemarque, "Returnal" follows astronaut and pilot Selene Vassos, who gets stranded on the mysterious alien planet Atropos. Selene quickly realizes that the planet is filled with hostile alien creatures and plagued by a distortion in time that causes her to loop back to her crash site every time she dies.

Selene has access to a melee weapon, but guns are the main focus of the third-person combat in "Returnal." Players can find increasingly powerful weapons and upgrade them as they progress through the three biomes of Atropos. Mastering the weapons is another story entirely, and anyone who charges into "Returnal" should be prepared to die a lot. That's part of the fun, though, and slowly upgrading Selene's arsenal while simultaneously sharpening your own skills and knowledge of alien life on Atropos is an extremely satisfying process.

"Returnal" is one of the games that make buying the PlayStation 5 worthwhile . The game has since been ported to PC, but unless you've got a starship's onboard computer sitting in your home office, "Returnal" plays best on console.

Bethesda Softworks "Intergalactic" is going to be an action-packed sci-fi adventure with a thrilling narrative, but Naughty Dog is far from the only studio to set its sights on the stars. "Starfield" is one of the biggest space games ever made, and it's filled with enough sidequests, alien worlds, and orbital combat to keep you busy for months on end. However, Bethesda games are typically much more open-ended and sprawling than Naughty Dog titles. We expect "Intergalactic" to be a more focused narrative experience than "Starfield," but Bethesda's massive galaxy looks and feels like it could slot right into the world shown in the "Intergalactic" reveal trailer.

If you've played any other Bethesda RPG, you've got a rough idea of what the "Starfield" experience is like. Players can customize a character before jumping into an expansive galaxy populated by multiple interstellar governments, explorers' organizations, and space pirate crews. The combat has a wealth of guns for players to choose from, but there's also an array of melee weapons that might help you warm up for Jordan A. Mun's swordfighting in "Intergalactic."

In our review of "Starfield," we sang the praises of one of the game's most unique and well-designed features: the ship builder. Any sci-fi fan is guaranteed to lose hours creating the perfect vessel for their space adventures, and that process might be worth the price of entry for "Starfield" all by itself.

Sony Interactive Entertainment We had to throw at least one other Naughty Dog game on our suggestion list. If you're impatiently awaiting the release of "Intergalactic," then you might as well get to know some of the developer's other work. For more than a decade, Naughty Dog has been something of a "The Last of Us" factory, but before that series made such a splash, the developer was known for a different action franchise.

The "Uncharted" series puts players right into the center of a summer blockbuster action movie. As treasure hunter Nathan Drake, players will need to explore ruins, solve ancient puzzles, and gun down enemies. Every "Uncharted" game offers a near-perfect balance of cover-based shooting and puzzle solving while also telling genuinely engaging stories that would feel right at home on the big screen (even if the eventual big screen adaptation didn't quite hit the mark).

Playing the first "Uncharted," which debuted on the PlayStation 3, requires a little extra legwork, but the "Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves" collection is a fantastic choice for anyone with a PS5. The set includes remastered versions of "Uncharted 4: A Thief's End," arguably the highlight of the series, and "Uncharted: The Lost Legacy." There's no better way to get a feel for the approach to storytelling and combat that we'll likely see in Naughty Dog's upcoming release.

CD Projekt Red "Intergalactic" is a sci-fi game that promises to have a strong narrative and addictive melee combat. Fortunately for impatient gamers, there's another semi-recent release that just so happens to be one of the best sci-fi games ever made. "Cyberpunk 2077" is a visually stunning and narratively rich experience that could easily help make a good chunk of time disappear while you wait for "Heretic."

The game doesn't have any third-person action, but it does have some of the slickest sci-fi swordplay we've ever seen. Make some room for time-dilating cyberware like the Sandevistan in your build, and you can play a cyber-ninja that dices up their enemies before anyone even knows you're in the battle. Of course, "Cyberpunk 2077" also has a full suit of ranged weapons and the option to digitally attack your enemies with quickhacks. And after you've exhausted your capacity for katana-wielding, the game still has plenty to offer.

items.title: Steam Cyberpunk Fest Is Full Of Hidden Gems And Modern Classics
items.summary: It’s time for another sale on PC games, and this time, you can strap in for Steam Cyberpunk Fest 2026, which shines a light on the games that celebrate the future and the inevitable dystopia we’re headed towards. Constant surveillance, corporations becoming national powers, and neon lighting are hallmarks of the genre, and plenty of...
items.content:
Gaming Gaming Deals Steam Cyberpunk Fest Is Full Of Hidden Gems And Modern Classics GameSpot Follow Darryn Bonthuys Mon, August 3, 2026 at 6:02 PM UTC Add us on Google Mon, August 3, 2026 at 6:02 PM UTC GameSpot may receive revenue from affiliate and advertising partnerships for sharing this content and from purchases through links.

It's time for another sale on PC games, and this time, you can strap in for Steam Cyberpunk Fest 2026, which shines a light on the games that celebrate the future and the inevitable dystopia we're headed towards. Constant surveillance, corporations becoming national powers, and neon lighting are hallmarks of the genre, and plenty of games have dipped their toes into that dark future. With so much to choose from, where does one even begin?

We've taken a look at the games on sale and dropped some of our picks below for a mix of hard-hitting futurism and atmospheric worldbuilding, all spread across various genres.

As a reminder, Steam Cyberpunk Fest runs August 3-10, and once it concludes, it'll be followed by Pins & Pegs Fest (August 17-20) and PvE Survival Crafting Fest (August 31 – September 7). For a closer look at what the rest of the year holds in store–as well as the first half of 2027–you can check out our feature on all the upcoming Steam sales .

We might as well start this list off with the biggest name in the genre, Cyberpunk 2077 and its phenomenal expansion Phantom Liberty . Almost six years after it first launched in a disastrous state, Cyberpunk 2077 has had numerous upgrades installed, polishing the game to a level where you genuinely feel like you're a citizen in a neon-soaked dystopian future. Strong on storytelling and buildcrafting gameplay where you fine-tune your Edgerunner, Cyberpunk 2077 gives you all the tools you need to be a Night City legend. And with a new anime series inspired by the game on the way, now is the perfect time to hop in and see what all the fuss is about.

The 2023 RoboCop game checks all the boxes for a cyberpunk game: You've got a corporation that has more power than elected officials, everything is baked in a neon glow, and gangs of criminals who are content to commit fashion crimes on top of the usual felonies. RoboCop: Rogue City not only nails that atmosphere, but also the feeling of being a cybernetic cop programmed to mete out justice by stylishly taking down every bad guy in CRT-scale sight with slick gunplay and brute machine force. The game also shines a light on what Alex Murphy does between cases, and the Unfinished Business expansion is a great standalone campaign that imagines RoboCop if it were an unofficial Raid movie.

It might look like a cyberpunk-themed version of Hotline Miami, but Kusan: City of Wolves successfully carves its own identity through bloody battles, a deep grid-based upgrade system, and an adrenaline-pumping soundtrack full of hard-hitting Korean hip-hop. Full of hardcore action where there's no room for error, the game is all about lightning-fast combat with the intensity dialed up to 11.

You can't spell cyberpunk without some of the letters in dystopia, and the Ghostrunner games are a fun blast of high-octane energy and parkour. Death is always a single blow away, but by the time you master the gameplay, you'll be a lean-and-mean killing machine who can wallrun and power-slide their way to victory. A synth-heavy electronic soundtrack and a game world that emphasizes the depressing nature of megacorps taking over society only adds to the techno-magic of these gems.

No list about cyberpunk games is truly complete without at least one title that focuses on hacking, and that's where Into the Grid earns its spot. If you're not jaded by the idea of playing a roguelike deckbuilder, then you'll appreciate how Into the Grid combines the genre with clever spatial strategy and resource management as you work your way through corporate servers. It's a neat twist on established deck-building tropes, and the tactical simulation of cyber-infiltration is given a sharp presentation.

You might have fantasized about living in a cyberpunk world, but have you ever considered building your own? Dystopika gives you all the tools you need to build the dystopia of tomorrow, without any of the megacorp pressure. It's the darker side of cozy city-building, as there are no goals or objectives to chase. Simply place buildings, erect giant billboards, and watch your metropolis come to life in this sci-fi zen game.

It's not cyberpunk, it's cyberfunk! A spiritual successor to Jet Set Radio, you play as an up-and-coming graffiti artist who has lost their head–literally. On a quest to reclaim your noggin, you'll get to explore several boroughs, tag the walls with spraycan art, and use extreme sports skills to evade the militarized police of a dark future. Full of smooth gameplay and a stellar soundtrack, you'll want to check this out if you've been pining for those halcyon Dreamcast days.

Hades developer Supergiant is best-known for its roguelite adventures featuring a pantheon of Greek gods and legends, but before it tasked players with escaping the underworld, it was combining emotions and action in Transistor. An elegant combo of art deco and cyberpunk themes, Transistor also fuses real-time combat with turn-based tactics as you take part in an emotional narrative driven by music.

Metal Eden doesn't chart new ground for boomer-shooters, but it still deserves praise for mixing satisfying moment-to-moment action with sharp cyberpunk style. If you're looking for fluid action, movement options that feel empowering, and a slick aesthetic, then you'll want to grab a download of this exciting and well-designed shooter.

There's something magical about the idea of a cyberpunk city, and in Cloudpunk, you'll get to explore the metropolis of the future from up high. You'd think that delivering packages in a future where you have access to gravity-defying cars would be easy, but with towering skyscrapers and corporate conspiracies dogging you, you have to keep your eyes on the prize. Cloudpunk nails the cyberpunk aesthetic with its art direction, and with dozens of interesting characters to meet and decisions that have a lasting impact on the world around you, it's a great game for anyone who enjoys that sci-fi atmosphere.

items.title: MacBook Neo opens 500-page Word doc much faster than comparable Windows notebook
items.content:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Future) Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Remember those 'I'm a Mac, and I'm a PC' ad spots from years ago? Such platform rivalry feels like old, mouldering hat these days (especially to a console-gaming interloper like me). That said, we live in a world where both the MacBook Neo and the Dell XPS 13, two notebooks alike in dignity, are vying for the crown of 'most affordable entry-level notebook' at $699 a piece.

The rivalry is old news, though a fresh twist in the tale is that apparently large Microsoft Word files actually open faster on the MacBook Neo. Independent testing carried out by PhoneBuff found that the Neo opened a 500-page Word document in a hair over 7 seconds, whereas a similarly specced Dell XPS 13 took 12 seconds (via Windows Latest ).

It's quite the upset—you'd think that after all these years, Microsoft would offer the optimum Word Doc experience within Windows. To add insult to injury, the MacBook Neo doesn't even have Apple's speedy M-series silicon, but instead features what is essentially a repurposed phone chip in the A18 Pro. Though, to be fair, this 'mere' phone chip is still comparable to older M-series chips.

Notebooks like this can handle more than just note-taking. The Dell XPS 13 features an Intel Core 5 320 (a stripped-down version of the Panther Lake chips we like a lot ), which should offer plenty of other opportunities to shine throughout PhoneBuff's testing. For instance, on startup the Dell XPS 13 races to the desktop in 24 seconds. The MacBook Neo takes very nearly twice as long, clocking in at 40 seconds. Mind you, that may not really be an, ahem, apples to apples comparsion as the notebooks are running two different operating systems.

But as both of the laptops tested were configured with only 8 GB of RAM, you'd perhaps expect this to be a closer run thing. PhoneBuff's battery efficiency and creative workload tests are a lot more variable, but there's only one thing that I'm interested in here: gaming performance.

Cyberpunk 2077 on a notebook? It's more likely than you think—though with some caveats, obviously. The MacBook Neo loaded up CD Projekt Red's techno dystopia in a hair under 41 seconds, whereas the Dell XPS 13 managed it in 55. When it comes to the game benchmark, though, you can't even attempt to run it at ultra settings on the Dell XPS 13.

Otherwise, when running fullscreen, the XPS 13 averages 16 fps in the benchmark, whereas the MacBook Neo averages almost 20 fps. Now, the MacBook Neo outperforming the Dell was not something I was expecting. Though I also wouldn't necessarily call 20 fps 'playable,' let alone 'enjoyable'.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Our Ian managed to get the MacBook Neo to run Cyberpunk 2077 at 30 FPS in his own testing earlier this year. He writes in his review , "The downside is that to get this, you need to dip below Steam Deck settings, using the Low graphics profile, with the resolution at 720p, and with MetalFX upscaling in performance mode. That's not great, and looks a little soft thanks to all the upscaling going on, but at least it is technically playable."

Personally, I think I'll be sticking with my rig for Cyberpunk 2077—though either notebook might still get a look in for less hardware-intensive indie releases and visual novels.

If you manage your gaming expectations accordingly, then the XPS 13's 13-inch OLED touch display is nothing to sneeze at. The XPS 13's OLED also enjoys P3 colour gamut, meaning it supports a slightly wider range of colours than the MacBook Neo. Furthermore, its 120 Hz refresh rate is twice that of the MacBook Neo's screen—at the very least, scrolling through a webpage will feel a smidge smoother on the Dell, even if its Intel Core 5 320 chip will struggle to keep up with your competitive favourites.

items.title: The 10 Best Video Game Worlds of All Time, Ranked
items.summary: Explore the best video game worlds of all time, ranked by design, storytelling, and quality, from Zelda
items.content:
By Lucas Kloberdanz-Dyck Published Aug 1, 2026, 5:41 PM EDT Lucas Kloberdanz-Dyck is a writer for Collider. He grew up creating lists, stories, and worlds, which led to his love of anime and video games. He attended Sheridan College where he earned an Honours Bachelor of Game Design. Lucas and his group won 1st place for technical innovation at LevelUp Toronto 2023, and he was also an intern for the Oakville Film Festival of Arts. Sign in to your Collider account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 6 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There are many reasons why people play video games. Some enjoy a cozy comfort game like Animal Crossing: New Horizons to sit back, relax, and de-stress. Others prefer an intense action extravaganza where the fight just doesn't stop, such as God of War . There are also gamers who like a masterfully written narrative that pushes the bounds of storytelling in video games, including The Last of Us .

No matter what type of game players like, including those three examples, they all had to have taken place in some sort of world . Game worlds encapsulate everything the title defines, from mechanics to design to narrative to the setting itself. Since it is such an important and immersive part of a game, this list will rank the best video game worlds of all time based on how iconic they are, design, influence, storytelling, interactivity, identity, originality, importance, lore, worldbuilding, scale, polish, detail, relevance to the game, and overall quality.

Kazuma Kiryu with a cigarette in his mouth walking down the street in the intro to 'Yakuza 0' Image via SEGA Just because they are called video game worlds doesn't mean they have to be sprawling continents. Some prove their excellence through a tight, citywide design, like Yakuza 0 and other games in the franchise. Set in Kamurocho, a neighborhood based on Tokyo's real-life Kabukicho district, this eccentric chunk of the city is home to bright lights, gambling, host clubs, and rampant crime.

Most games within the Yakuza franchise are set within Kamurocho, so by the time players get caught up to the most recent entry, they will have memorized the layout, knowing the district at heart. It slowly evolves and changes over time, adding to the skyline, some businesses closing down, and changing styles to fit the decade. Kamurocho is a dynamic world with plenty of flashy things to do, creating a sense of home.

Two trainers stare at Mount Coronet, surrounded by Pokémon Image via the Pokémon Company If fans were to choose what video game world they would want to live in, most people would select some sort of region in Pokémon , and that is because all of them are full of childlike wonder and nostalgia. First introduced in Pokémon Diamond and Pearl , the world was perfected in Pokémon Platinum , with gamers traveling around the northern terrain in order to catch the temporal legendaries and defeat the Champion.

Even though this list is selecting Sinnoh, any Pokémon region deserves to be on this list. Sinnoh was always a fan-favorite ever since the first games, boasting unique lore that established ancient history within the franchise. But after Pokémon Legends: Arceus came out and introduced Hisui, the world became that much better, allowing players to explore an open-world variant which they can compare to the modern one, proving why it is such a replayable Pokémon video game .

Grand Theft Auto V - 2013 Image via Rockstar Games Grand Theft Auto VI is the most anticipated video game of all time, and fans finally get to play it sooner than ever. While it is taking players back into Vice City, for now, the best setting in the franchise is Los Santos from Grand Theft Auto V . This city is a parody version of Los Angeles, with Trevor, Franklin, and Michael all teaming up to pull off a series of high-stakes heists throughout the city.

All the Grand Theft Auto games have incredible worlds, but as the most recent one, Los Santos is bigger and better than ever in terms of scale, polish, graphics, and things to do. As a sandbox game, one of the main selling points is its city full of emergent gameplay, with players mixing their curiosity with guns, cars, unique physics, and whatever landmark they see. It facilitates player freedom and chaotic choices while also being revered for its detailed depiction of Los Angeles.

open-world-xbox-one-games-cyberpunk-2077.jpg Image via CD Projekt Red Mike Pondsmith created Night City for his board game, and while it was already excellent, Cyberpunk 2077 brought it into video game format for all fans to enjoy. Night City is in no shortage of criminals and punks, but that seems to be the only way to make a living in this futuristic hellhole. V is one such punk who tries to get a microchip with the mind of a terrorist out of their brain before it is too late.

Cyberpunk 2077 features some of the most fascinating worldbuilding in video game history and the implications of capitalism and greed on the future and how it affects the city itself, and in turn, the people. Night City can be looked at as a character itself, mainly because it is directly used as a character development and narrative tool to progress the story. The vertical design and dense world offer a jam-packed feeling that is the pinnacle of cyberpunk, highlighting its excellence through societal divides and cultural influences.

elden-ring-erdtree.jpg Image via Bandai Namco Entertainment Fantasy video games have some of the best worlds in the medium because they always offer a grand sense of adventure with no shortage of worldbuilding and lore. The Lands Between from Elden Ring is no different. This perilous world is home to a rich history and terrifying monsters, including the demi-god children of Queen Marika, who claimed the shards of the titular object for themselves.

The juxtaposition of charming fantasy wonder and grotesque monster horrors is what sets Elden Ring apart from other fantasy games, somehow capturing both feelings of darkness and whimsy. Without any map markers, players are taught to get lost in this world, with curiosity driving them to new landmarks and puzzles . Pair this with immensely detailed and intriguing lore, and Elden Ring proves why it is such a masterpiece, especially because of how visually stunning The Lands Between is.

Your answers point to the world your instincts were built for. This is the universe your temperament, your survival instincts, and your particular brand of stubbornness were made for.

You took the red pill a long time ago — probably before anyone offered it to you. You're a systems thinker who can't help but notice the seams in things.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 meets Disco Elysium in stunning Steam RPG taster available now
items.summary: It feels like this game was made specifically for Cyberpunk 2077 and Disco Elysium fans
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 and Disco Elysium, check out this Steam freebie

If you’re a fan of the RPG games Cyberpunk 2077 and Disco Elysium , then you need to download this free Steam demo ahead of its full launch in August.

When it comes to sci-fi RPGs, it doesn't get much better than CD Projekt RED’s Cyberpunk 2077 . An immersive RPG inspired by Ridley Scott’s Blade Runner , where you go from rags to riches in the seedy world of Night City, home to the most sinister criminal scum there ever were. Along with you, of course.

Considering its woeful launch in 2020, it’s amazing how the developers at CDPR have not only risen this game like a phoenix from the ashes, but it’s fair to say that many promises have long overdelivered when it comes to Cyberpunk 2077 .

Then we have Disco Elysium , a cult classic indie game where you get to play detective in an enticing noir setting of Revachol, and much like Cyberpunk 2077 , it offered players many ways to approach situations, making each playthrough different from the last.

That all being said, one may be an AAA big hitter and the other an indie darling, but few would deny that Cyberpunk 2077 and Disco Elysium aren't two of the best RPGs in recent years.

READ MORE: 10 highly anticipated new games coming to PC in August 2026

If you’re a fan of either, then you’re going to want to check out the upcoming indie RPG, Kill the Shadow , developed by Shadowlight. It’s a sci-fi detective RPG with a gorgeous pixel art style.

“Kill the Shadow is a detective game with multiple endings, featuring 2.5D pixel art and semi-open exploration and investigation,” reads the description of the game on Steam. “Play as Lucas, a former police officer, alongside a mysterious Shadow who can see the “past.” Remember—every choice you make will change the fate of countless characters!”

If Kill the Shadow looks like it could be your cup of tea, then you’ll be pleased to know that you can download its free playable demo right now on Steam.

While it's too early for reviews, it seems like Kill the Shadow has been receiving early praise from the community far.

“ Kill the Shadow was one of my favourite demos of Next Fest, and I highly recommend checking it out,” said The Gamer.

“Hope this game gets more traction. It has a gorgeous art style and interesting gameplay,” commented a hopeful user on YouTube.

“Praying for a console port in future,” pleaded ePai9e.

items.title: I have FOMO for the worst era of Cyberpunk 2077
items.summary: Bring gear stats and ripperdoc-specific cyberware back to the RPG
items.content:
Bring gear stats and ripperdoc-specific cyberware back to the RPG's sequel!

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A few months after Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty launched alongside v2.0, I stepped into Night City for the very first time . The experience was baffling. If I wasn't puzzling over the different kinds of operating systems and playstyles, I was getting an eyeful of every townie's butt cheeks as they strutted about Watson looking like randomized Sims. I powered through the weirdness and learned to embrace it, going on to complete it three times in less than six months.

Anything I didn't understand was chalked up to being a newbie. The lack of handholding or mechanic explanations confounded me at first, but I reminded myself that I was playing a three-year-old RPG for the first time. Maybe developer CD Projekt Red saw no need to tutorialize it too much for the hordes of returning fans, I wondered?

Only now, on my fifth playthrough, has curiosity finally gotten the better of me. One YouTube rabbit hole later thanks to videos like this , I've been confronted with how incredibly different this game was at launch. Not just in terms of being far more stable and less prone to bugs and crashes these days, but in the evolution of some pretty interesting mechanics and systems that I honestly wish I'd gotten to experience for myself. Cyberpunk 2, take note please.

I bounced off of Cyberpunk 2077 for 2 months when I first played it, and that makes it perfect for Xbox Game Pass

I adore games that let me diva out . I want to be the most dripped-out baddie in the Badlands, so it makes sense that one of my biggest draws into the world of Cyberpunk 2077 was V's impressive wardrobe. I made it my mission from day-one to traverse every nook and cranny of Night City in search of the coolest threads V could lay her chromed-out hands on, and for the most part, I succeeded. One thing I shrugged off on my hunt for sartorial supremacy was the fact that clothing items, much like weapons or cyberware, are color-coded into tier grades. In the end I'd just assumed it was a Night City classist thing; grey tier-one gear was simply the cheap bargain bin stuff I'd start out with, while orange tier 5 pieces might run me a few more eddies in exchange for looking like street punk royalty. It wasn't until I finally took it upon myself to research why clothing items are tiered despite only being cosmetics that I started to feel left out.

Surprise, surprise: the color-coded tier levels on clothing items in Cyberpunk 2077 are a vestige from a time when they did serve a greater purpose. Once upon a time, gear could be crafted out of tiered parts just like quickhacks, weapons, and grenades, granting V different buffs and armor values depending on the tier level. They even had mod slots!

Cyberpunk 2077 has finally made me the corpo baddie of my RPG dreams and I regret everything already Six years later, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners season 2 wraps gaming's greatest comeback story With no combat system, Zero Parades is an RPG all about skill checks and spycraft, and it's more exciting for it

This resulted in some truly, uh, interesting fashion choices as players sought to min-max the hell out of their gear (as you can see from the vintage screenshot above, circa-2021). Transmog didn't exist at all, so it was perfectly acceptable to slink into a stealthy thief gig dressed to the nines in stilettos, a polka dot bra, and a hideous fluorescent beanie.

Suddenly, it all made sense. I feel highly privileged to be playing a version of the game that looks and feels fantastic, but there's something fittingly absurd about mercs cutting about Corpo Plaza like a half-dressed Barbie doll found in a dumpster. Sometimes I feel bad for being the only fashionable person in Night City as it is; how could these commoners possibly compete with Queen V's perfectly coordinated red, black, and gold outfits? But in another life, I, too, was meant to be clad in mesh vests and office slacks. Maybe I'm the weird one for sticking out like a sore thumb after all.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

This is not me championing for CDPR to bring back a transmog-less world in Cyberpunk 2077. I'd sooner zero myself than let Judy see me in stained sneakers. But I do wonder how it would have felt to play the game relying on my gear to actually power me up rather than adding yet more weight and importance to the ever-grindy path of cyberware leveling instead.

It's too easy to be the most chromed out queen this side of the Blackwall, let alone the best-dressed merc.

In 2015, Polish video game developer and publisher CD Projekt Red was at the top of the gaming industry. Hot off the release of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , which was largely considered one of the best games of all time, gamers couldn’t wait to see the developers’ next project.

And at Gamescom 2018, CD Projekt Red released a full trailer and pre-alpha gameplay for its next title, Cyberpunk 2077 , which was released on December 10, 2020, following numerous delays.

Now that the game is out, it has been mired in controversy. The primary issue is that Cyberpunk was released in a lacklustre state on the Xbox One and PS4, leading to numerous patches, an apology from the head of the company , and an unprecedented refund policy .

However, on a proper gaming PC (or PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X), and thanks to those patches (and others on the way), Cyberpunk boasts an incredible setting, engaging plot, and compelling gameplay worthy of the CD Projekt Red pedigree.

The game takes place in Night City, an American megacity located in California and entirely controlled by corporations. And it takes inspiration from the Cyberpunk tabletop role-playing game created by Mike Pondsmith. Pondsmith, in turn, was inspired by seminal science fiction authors such as William Gibson ( Neuromancer ), and Phillip K. Dick ( Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? ), whose influence you can feel in the game world.

Players assume the role of V, a fully customizable mercenary who can assume three different classes: NetRunner (hacking), Techie (machinery), and Solo (combat). After selecting a class, V assumes one of three life paths: Nomad, Streetkid, or Corpo (corporate). These life paths add exclusive missions to the game, including a unique prologue, and they affect how characters interact with you in the game world.

After you create your customized V, you can start the game's plot. Given that Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the most ambitious open-world games ever created, you’ll experience a lot of the plot via exploration. However, Cyberpunk 2077 's main story involves various heists and betrayals around Night City, during which you’ll become close to legendary in-universe rock star Johnny Silverhand, portrayed by none other than Keanu Reeves.

There are three other types of quest structures beyond the main story. The first is the side quest, which you can find in most modern RPGs. The side quests in Cyberpunk 2077 are structured to tell the story of a specific community or location within Night City.

There are more than 90 side quests in the game, and some have branching storylines across multiple missions. You can find many of them just by traversing Night City and interacting with different NPCs.

There are also more than 85 gig missions and more than 15 Cyberpsycho sighting missions available. These missions are contract-based and allow you to interact with the game world in a less story-driven way.

Gigs come in several forms, including assassinations, fetch quests, sabotage, and search and rescue. Each gig quest type caters to a certain style of play, and you can access them once you enter a new area of Night City.

Cyberpsycho sightings, on the other hand, are essentially mini-boss fights that put your combat skills to the test. If you played The Witcher 3 , they largely resemble that game’s monster hunts.

items.title: The new CyberPunk 2077 game is more analogue than you might think
items.summary: You might want to get on board.
items.content:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter If you're a fan of CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077, you might have been excited about some of the headlines appearing in the past couple of days. 'New Cyberpunk 2077 game reveals official gameplay,' one read. ‘Cyberpunk 2077 returns with ambitious new release,' was another. One even suggested that a new Cyberpunk 2077 was going to steal GTA 6's thunder.

Alas, some fans might have been disappointed to read those stories and discover that the new game is more analogue than what they might have imagined. Given how long it takes to make an AAA video game, it was highly unlikely that we would get Cyberpunk 2077 2 in 2027 – 2028 maybe, but even that's a very optimistic estimate.

The new Cyberpunk 2077 is, in fact, a board game. But don't write it off, it follows in a long traditional of video game to board game transitions, and some of them have been quite good.

Watch On Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game looks set to do justice to the video game's vast lore and worldbuilding in its physical scale. The eight-minute unboxing video above reveals just how huge it is with the various miniatures, mission cards, character boards and gameplay expansions

Published by Go On Board, it's billed as a cooperative, story-driven campaign game. Players take on the roles of Edgerunners, exploring Night City and completing 13 multi-stage missions. A timer mechanic is intended to replicate the paced of the action of the video game.

Board of Prime Day?! There's a board game for that GTA 6 could be the final death knell for physical media Hear me out, GTA 6's graphics might be too good The game follows the release of the trading card game Cyberpunk TCG. If its successful, it should be able to evolve alongside the video game franchise for many years.

The trend of turning video games into board games has exploded over the past decade, with crowdfunding platforms like Kickstarter or Gamefound playing a big role in helping the physical adaptations get off the ground. They also tap into the growing interest in physical media and analogue tech as a respite from digital screen time, providing a physical social experience.

Critical reception has been a bit of a mixed bag. Some have been heralded as masterpieces, others are criticised as overpriced miniature-fests that prioritise plastic over playable design.

The most successful adaptations are those that don't just copy-paste the digital game, but translate its feeling and core loops into smart, physical mechanics. Slay the Spire: The Board Game is much loved for how it turned a single-player digital roguelike and turning it into cooperative tabletop deck-builder, and Frostpunk succeeded in bringing the punishing decision-making of digital survival games to the table.

On a very different note, the cosy Dorfromantik: The Board Game captured the zen-like puzzle game vibe of its digital counterpart.

How Cyberpunk 2077 accidentally inspired this gorgeous anime football platformer Fans want to send this new Stranger Things spin-off back to the Upside Down How one video game brought me back to gaming after 15 years On the other hand, Dark Souls: The Board Game was seen by some as being tedious and repetitive despite its gorgeous miniatures.

Board games can also be the ultimate collector's item for video game fans. Even if a $200 Elden Ring or Resident Evil board games only hits the table once or twice a year, the gorgeous, highly detailed miniatures also serve as display pieces.

You can find out more about Cyberpunk 2077 The Board Game on the Go On Board website.

items.title: Five Years Of ‘Cyberpunk 2077,’ My Favorite Game Of All Time
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 is my favorite game of all time, and as it celebrates five years since release, I reflect on what it meant to me.
items.content:
Gaming Five Years Of ‘Cyberpunk 2077,’ My Favorite Game Of All Time By Paul Tassi ,

Forbes contributors publish independent expert analyses and insights. News and opinion about video games, television, movies and the internet. Follow Author Dec 11, 2025, 10:24am EST Cyberpunk 2077 CDPR “What’s your favorite game?” It’s a simple question that you would imagine someone who writes about video games for a living would have an answer to. But it’s always been a tough one. Halo 3 ? Maybe Mass Effect 2 ? Super Smash Bros. 64 ? Destiny 2, the game I’ve sunk 5,000 hours into?

I never had a clear answer until a few years ago, when I suddenly realized that after four playthroughs and hundreds of hours, it was Cyberpunk 2077 , which just celebrated its fifth anniversary this week.

It feels improbable. I loved The Witcher 3 , which was my first experience with CDPR, and as such, I was interested in Cyberpunk 2077 , albeit perhaps with less enthusiasm than some. But the game was released and consumed by one of the wildest launch stories ever, a disastrous release of an unbaked game mired with technical issues to the point where it was actually delisted from the PlayStation store for months, something almost never seen in the industry. It was broken broken.

Well, for some. Sure, I had bugs on PC in those early days, and performance could have been better, but it was certainly better than running it on console. And if you could block out the noise of the larger controversies, you could see it. You could see the core of this game was great, and if it had fixed things, added things, delivered on its full potential, it could have been great.

Cyberpunk 2077 CDPR Play Puzzles & Games on Forbes FEATURED | Frase By Forbes ™

It is great, now. CDPR spent at least two years getting the game to where it should have been at launch, but in the five-year span, it has dramatically overhauled most major systems in the game, particularly its skill trees. It also then released Phantom Liberty, where at that point, I was not all that surprised it became my favorite DLC of all time, as well.

Cyberpunk 2077 is simply best in class across so many categories. Night City is one of the best realized environments I’ve ever seen across any open world title, beating out Grand Theft Auto handily in terms of a gorgeous, living space (that got more convincing with patches to civilians and traffic, in time).

The voicework here is stellar. Yes, the star feature was Keanu Reeves, but there is no question in my mind that Cherami Leigh’s V is the best first-person narrator I’ve seen in a game. The concept of every bit of the game, even cutscenes, taking place in first person only worked because of her (and Male V, Gavin Drea, was solid as well). Leigh’s performance, however praised, was not praised enough.

The excellent voicework extends to the excellent characters and the writing to bring them to life. In particular, Judy and Panam quickly became some of my favorite video game NPCs, with Panam in particular being an unforgettable love interest that would make Mass Effect and Baldur’s Gate players jealous. Even if she rejected me. How many NPCs have ever broken your heart?

Cyberpunk 2077 CDPR None of this would work if the game itself was not fun. It was solid enough to start, but when Cyberpunk 2077 really kicked into gear was after its major skills overhaul. Half the reason I made four(!) different Vs was not just to make different story decisions, but to commit to different pathways and builds. I had my pure melee build (stupidly overpowered), my run and gun shotgun, LMG tank build, my hacking-only build full of exploding heads and cyberpsychosis, and finally, my final and favorite run, throwing knives only, like some sort of Goldeneye modifier. I don’t think there’s a better metaphor for Cyberpunk’s transformation than the original throwing knife skill being throwing a literal, single knife in your inventory, then needing to find it afterward lest you lose it. After the grand skill tree rework patch, it was switched to being a cooldown with infinite ammo, and it ended up being one of the most hilarious, legitimately strong builds in the game thanks to CDPR investing in the idea, rather than abandoning it.

Again, I made four Vs for four full runs of the game, at least until I was told to meet Hanako at Embers, as I’d done most of the endings by that point already. I have never done that many playthroughs of a single-player game before, and none of them felt like a slog. Ultimately I made my way to a new, “true," ending in Phantom Liberty which was one of the most gut-wrenching sequences I can remember in a game.

Something happened midway through these five years that changed my perception of all this. After blacking out, falling and smacking my head a number of times, I was diagnosed with epilepsy in my 30s, a rarity. Now, every time V’s brain glitched out because of the relic, and she found herself going dark and hitting the floor, I could feel that kind of pain and confusing. She was marching toward her death, I am not (well, technically I could die from one of these), but there is something to be said here about how Cyberpunk deals with grief and bravery in the face of illness (read my friend Gene Park’s essay about how he connected to Cyberpunk via his own cancer diagnosis).

Cyberpunk 2077 CDPR There is still lost potential in Cyberpunk . The idea of three different lifepaths never really manifested. The romance options, while compelling, are locked and limited. Johnny can be…a lot, if you ask me. But no game is perfect. Where it shines, it doesn’t just shine, it stands up to the greats in video game history and as such, is a great itself. For me, the greatest.

items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]

items.title: Update 2.3 Patch Notes
items.summary: Update 2.3 lands tomorrow! Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as sup
items.content:
Update 2.3 lands tomorrow!

Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as support for AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation, Intel XeSS 2.0 and HDR10+ Gaming, among others.

Update 2.3 also brings Cyberpunk 2077 to a whole new platform: Mac with Apple silicon! If you already own the game on Steam, you can play it on your compatible device. To find out whether your Mac can run Cyberpunk 2077, please check the official requirements.

Read the list of changes for more info:

Vehicles

  • Added 4 new vehicles, including several Side Jobs tied to acquiring them:

    • Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Hunt and The Beast In Me).

      An additional side job unlocks the CrystalCoat™ feature for it.

      [/*]

    • Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred"

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Beast in Me: Badlands, The Beast in Me: Santo Domingo, Transmission, and Search and Destroy)."

      [/*]

    • Yaiba ASM-R250 Muramasa

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, purchase 1 Yaiba vehicle, purchase at least 3 vehicles through AUTOFIXER, and complete Reported Crime: You Play with Fire...).

      If you fail the side job, the vehicle can later be purchased through AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]

    • Chevillon Legatus 450 Aquila

      Available for purchase on AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Introducing AutoDrive! This cutting-edge, autonomous driving feature will take you to your chosen destination (i.e. job objective or placed pin on the map). If you have no set destination, it will take you on a leisurely ride through the streets of Night City. Simply hop in any of your vehicles, make sure you're on a road, and hold G (PC) / Left Stick (consoles) to activate. This feature is disabled when you enter combat or when your vehicle is heavily damaged.

    [/*]

  • Implemented Cinematic Camera for AutoDrive. Hold Q (PC) / D-Pad Right (consoles) to activate. Sit back and enjoy cinematic views of Night City as you cruise toward your destination.

    [/*]

  • Self-driving Delamain cabs are now available on demand! Simply open the menu to call vehicles, then select "Delamain Cab" from the list to request a ride. This feature unlocks after completing the job Don't Lose Your Mind (regardless of outcome) and receiving a message from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ is now available for vehicles from partner brands, including motorcycles. Additionally, the infamous hacker known as Cosmetic_Troll exploited a vulnerability and created a cracked version of Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ technology for lower-end vehicles. Please note, however, that some models do not support the technology, such as heavily modded nomad vehicles and job-related vehicles.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color schemes did not work properly on the Mizutani Shion MZ1 and MZ2.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color scheme could not be applied properly to the Villefort Deleon "Vindicator".

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Added 27 new NPCs that can be spawned in Photo Mode, including Rita Wheeler, the Cassel twins, fixers, Dum Dum, the iguana, Brendan, and more.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between alternative outfits for NPCs spawned in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between V's saved Wardrobe outfits in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Added a confirmation pop-up when exiting Photo Mode to prevent accidental exits after setting up the perfect shot.

    [/*]

  • Added more customization options to the Look-At Camera feature, including an option for only the character's eyes to turn toward the camera instead of their entire body.

    [/*]

  • Added improvements to Lighting:

    • Lights now spawn around the camera instead of the player character.

      [/*]

    • Added an outline to the spotlight mesh and an indicator when it's off screen for better visibility.

      [/*]

    • Improved light movement speed on controllers.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Added multiple new stickers and frames, including iconic quotes and stylish overlays that let you turn your screenshots into Night City postcards – perfect for sharing memories from the City of Dreams.

    [/*]

  • Improved Depth of Field and moved it to the Camera tab.

    [/*]
